newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-PROCHAZKA HITS TWO AS CZECHS OVERCOME FINNS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-PROCHAZKA HITS TWO AS CZECHS OVERCOME FINNS.

text.p: Martin Prochazka scored twice as holders the Czech Republic beat hosts Finland 2-1 at the world ice hockey championship on Sunday.
Repeating their performance against Germany on Saturday, the Czechs came from behind to snatch their second one-goal victory.
"This was very important for us," said Czech coach Slavomir Lener. "We shook off early nervousness and the team felt very confident. We wanted to play very actively and aggressively."
Mika Nieminen opened the scoring for the Finns but Prochazka equalised with a thundering slapshot with less than a minute to play of the first period.
Prochazka scored the winner in the 42nd minute, hitting a backhand shot into an empty goal with Finnish keeper Jarmo Myllys stranded after failing to intercept a bouncing puck.

Finland head coach Curt Lindstrom called the ricochet which completely fooled Myllys "a quirk of fate". He said the puck had bounced unpredictably out of the goalkeeper's reach after hitting a nail protruding from the plank.
But Lindstrom did not blame the incident for the defeat.
"I think these Czechs are better than the team who won the world championship a year ago," he said.
Lener declined to comment on the comparison, but said "almost everything is still in front of us, we must stay concentrated and prepare well for our next two games".
The Czechs rest on Monday and Tuesday and play their neighbours Slovakia on Wednesday and Russia on Thursday.
